preliminaryLessons: Several major winners showed simultaneous operating acceleration and improving/raised outlooks before April 1.
Several major losers already showed weak growth, margin deterioration, or soft forward guidance before April 1.
Strong business DNA alone produced dangerous false positives: APP, FICO, and INTU require expectations, concentration/disruption, valuation, and market-confirmation gates.

Point-in-time valuation adds useful separation in at least one early pair: DELL traded near 19.4x trailing earnings on April 1 while APP carried a roughly 24.8x price/sales multiple at March 31 despite both showing strong operating growth.
The loser side contains several genuinely strong businesses (PODD, CSGP, BSX, ROL, APP), proving that Business DNA alone is insufficient.
Clear losers often advertised deterioration before April (DOW, CHTR, LULU, TSCO), supporting explicit Anti-DNA penalties.
Several winners were not classic growth stories (ILMN, HUM, CRL, CNC), so V2 needs turnaround/catalyst archetypes rather than one universal growth template.
The strongest clean operating-acceleration winners (MU, SNDK, DELL, AMD, CRWD, FLEX, BE) combined strong current growth with visible forward demand or raised/improving expectations.
Intel and Moderna prove that some six-month Monsters are catalyst/turnaround cases that would fail a pure operating-growth screen; archetype matters.
HII, NFLX, NRG, PODD, CSGP, BSX, APP and ROL are strong-business losers that must be explained by expectations, valuation, event risk or market confirmation rather than weak fundamentals.
Clear operating deterioration remains useful rejection evidence, but it is not sufficient to solve the hard false-positive cases.
